label: late "o" input in sequences starting with "f", after k/t/y
explanation: Very sparse conjunction feature that fires only in the original phase (t=4-8, mostly t=5-7), almost always (about 88% of steps, 95% of mass) when the input is "o". 98% of the mass is in sequences whose first token is "f". Activations are larger when k, t or y came one or two steps before (prev_tok k/t lift about 10x). It never fires during the delimiter or copy phases, even when "o" is copied back. Predicate "o" & first=f & t>=5 covers 91% of mass but has only 6% precision: most late "o"s in f-initial sequences stay silent. Adding a k/t/y-in-last-two-steps condition gives 24% precision and 82% mass. The remaining selectivity is unexplained, so this is not fully captured. A few weak activations fall on other tokens (h, j, w) right before an "o" slot, or on "o" in sequences that do not start with f. The largest activation (2.25) is f f d k k w [o].
